learning_outcomes.text: Has theoretical knowledge about phenomena in materials used in modern electrical engineering constructions and the properties of these materials
Knows basic methods, techniques, materials, and technologies used in the design and creation of electrical devices
Is able to combine knowledge about material structure with application in electrical constructions
Is aware of responsibility for their own work and readiness to abide by team work principles and take responsibility for jointly realized tasks

syllabus_topics: Constructions of low and high voltage electrical devices (2 hours)
Dependence of resistivity of conducting materials on temperature (4 hours)
Studies of electrical-thermal dependence of conductors in a wide range of temperatures (4 hours)
Determination of volume and surface resistivity of solid electro-insulating materials (4 hours)
Permittivity and dielectric loss factor of insulating materials (4 hours)
Studies of thermistor properties (2 hours)
Determination of characteristics of nonlinear resistors (4 hours)
Studies of magnetic material properties (4 hours)

Applications of materials in electrical engineering (1 hour) Overview of applications of conducting, insulating, magnetic and semiconductor materials - examples from power engineering, electronics, telecommunications. Influence of materials on technical progress in electrical engineering. Characteristics of materials used in generating, transmission and distribution devices.

Electromagnetic nature of material structure (2 hours) Material constants. Classification of materials used in electrical engineering. Structure of a solid. Influence of structure and composition of materials on their properties.

Properties of conducting materials (2 hours) Theories of electrical conductivity of metals, Matthiessen's rule. Comparison of properties of copper and aluminum. Dependence of conductivity of conducting materials on temperature. Atomic heat and conductivity of metals.

Characteristics of resistive and contact materials (2 hours) Mechanical properties of materials. Characteristics of resistive and contact materials. Types and properties of binders and solders. Thermal properties of metals. Causes and types of metal corrosion. Anti-corrosion protection of materials.

Special conducting materials (2 hours) Mechanism of Seebeck and Peltier thermoelectric phenomena. Parameters of materials used for thermocouples and thermopiles. Properties and applications of thermo-bimetals. Structure and properties of superconducting materials. Critical parameters of low and high temperature superconductors. Current and prospective applications of superconductors in electrical engineering.

Basic physical phenomena in dielectrics (2 hours) Structure of insulating materials. Mechanism of current conduction in dielectrics. Mechanisms of dielectric breakdown. Essence of polarization phenomenon and its consequences. Energy losses in insulating materials and methods of their determination. Optical properties of materials.

Determination of dielectric characteristics (2 hours) Studies of electrical strength of insulating materials. Measurement of permittivity and dielectric loss factor. Determination of volume and surface resistivity of dielectrics. Temperature dependence of resistivity of insulating materials and its consequences for operation.

Properties of insulating materials (2 hours) Types and properties of solid insulating materials. Structure, electrical and thermal properties of polymers. Application of polymers in the construction of electrical devices. Characteristics of ceramic, composite, mixture and layered systems materials. Classification, properties and application of insulating oils. Insulating properties of gases and their application in devices.

Phenomena in semiconductors (2 hours) Structure of semiconductor materials. Mechanism of electrical charge carrier formation. Influence of dopants on semiconductor material properties. Mechanism of current conduction in semiconductors. Influence of temperature on conductivity of semiconductor materials. Thermal dependencies of semiconductor conductivity. Essence of Hall effect, luminescence and their utilization.

Semiconductor material technologies (2 hours) Raw materials used for semiconductor material production. Methods of monocrystal production. Methods of cleaning semiconductor materials. Semiconductor doping technologies. Properties of p-n junctions and technologies of their production.

Application of semiconductor materials in electrical engineering (2 hours) Macroscopic structure and current conduction mechanism in varistors. Typical voltage-current dependencies of varistors and their basic parameters. Determination of voltage-current characteristics of varistors. Technological process of varistors. Materials used, characteristics and applications of thermistors. Utilization of p-n junction properties.

Magnetic properties of materials (2 hours) Essence of diamagnetism, paramagnetism and ferromagnetism. Magnetization process of ferromagnetic materials. Magnetocrystalline anisotropy. Typical magnetization curves of ferromagnets. Hysteresis loop of magnetic materials: basic parameters. Methods for determining magnetic permeability of ferromagnets. Influence of temperature on ferromagnet properties. Essence of magnetostriction phenomenon and its utilization.

Soft magnetic materials in devices (2 hours) Basic properties of soft magnetic materials. Types of magnetic materials used in electrical engineering. Production of silicon sheets. Technological process of amorphous materials. Properties of silicon sheets and amorphous materials and their application. Mechanisms of energy loss generation in ferromagnets. Methods of reducing losses in cores of electrical devices.

Characteristics of properties of hard and unconventional magnetic materials (2 hours) Technological processes of hard magnetic materials. Influence of process parameters on material structure and properties. Properties of hard magnetic materials and their application. Unconventional magnetic materials. Basic properties and application of magnetic liquids.

Development directions in material engineering (1 hour) Methods of obtaining, properties and application of fullerenes and carbon nanotubes. Electro-optical phenomena in materials. Optoelectronics and fiber optic technologies. Development directions of material engineering: nanotechnologies, material bioengineering, smart materials, quantum electronics and spintronics.
assessment_rules: Lectures are verified by an examination. Laboratory classes are verified by a test, which can be oral or written, and credit is based on presenting a solution to the given problem. Passing the module requires passing all laboratory classes.
